name: rag-qa-system golden set v1
description: Curated Q&A pairs over the sample docs corpus. relevant_sources lists the document filenames (as indexed) that a correct retrieval MUST surface.

items.question: What is RAG and why is it used?
items.expected: RAG stands for Retrieval-Augmented Generation. It combines a retriever that fetches relevant passages from a knowledge base with a generator that conditions its answer on those passages, reducing hallucination and grounding answers in source data.

items.question: What is the difference between chunking by character count and semantic chunking?
items.expected: Character-count chunking cuts text at fixed intervals and can split mid-sentence, destroying meaning. Semantic chunking splits on sentence or paragraph boundaries and merges up to a target size, preserving meaning within each chunk.

items.question: Which vector database is recommended for under 10 million vectors?
items.expected: pgvector is fine for under 10 million vectors. For larger or specialized workloads, Pinecone, Weaviate, or Qdrant are common choices.

items.question: What does recall@k measure in a retrieval system?
items.expected: recall@k measures the fraction of relevant items that appear in the top-k retrieved results. It is a retrieval-only metric evaluated before any generation step.

items.question: Why use a cross-encoder for reranking instead of a bi-encoder?
items.expected: A cross-encoder scores query and passage together so they attend to each other, giving better relevance estimates than a bi-encoder. It is slower, so it is used as a second stage after fast bi-encoder retrieval.

items.question: What is Reciprocal Rank Fusion and why use it for hybrid search?
items.expected: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) combines rankings from multiple retrievers using 1/(k+rank). It needs no score normalization, making it robust for fusing BM25 and dense scores that live on different scales.

items.question: What is a hallucination in the context of RAG answers?
items.expected: A hallucination is content in the generated answer that is not supported by the retrieved context. Faithfulness measures the fraction of answer tokens grounded in the context.

items.question: What are the trade-offs of a smaller chunk size?
items.expected: Smaller chunks improve retrieval precision because each chunk is more focused, but they may fragment context needed to answer synthesis questions. Overlap helps preserve continuity across boundaries.
